utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You took into account and accepted the ICMP list with its identification numbers and profiles, but for some reason you combined with those findings the names taken from the ICRC instead of the ICMP. Can you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it's a combination of both. These two lists were cross-referenced by our demographic unit and they found out that on the ICMP list there are people who are included into the ICRC missing list. So it's, yes, a combination of both lists. But what I was counting for my report, I extracted individuals which I found on the ICMP list, because on the ICRC list there are still people, individuals, who are reported missing and have not yet been identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did you give preference to the ICRC list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way I didn't give priority to any of those two sources, but they are different sources. For example, ICRC list has been compiled closer to the event, after the fall of Srebrenica, whereas on the other hand the ICMP commenced its work in 2001. Also on the ICRC list you would get certain information more accurate than on the ICMP list. I think I told yesterday that on the ICRC list you will find the date and place of this disappearance more accurate than on the ICMP list. So that's why you have to take into consideration both lists, but those two lists were examined in details by demographic unit, and I think there are experts who will testify in this trial if they haven't yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I understood correctly when you say "our demographic units," you mean the demographic units of the OTP; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I was having in mind Mr. Helge Brunborg and Ms. Ewa Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What else should be taken from the ICMP list into that combination rather than something else?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understand what you are asking. Can you perhaps clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I must say I'm a bit concerned. If we have a menu of things that we like and that we don't like, and then we take a bit from the ICRC and replace with it something from the ICMP list, this mix of apples and oranges - if I can say so - is a bit inconsistent. Did you take only the names from the ICRC list or something else as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Starting from your previous answer, whether witness was giving preference to the ICRC list, I do not understand where the witness has taken the names from the ICRC list. But in any event, do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will try to explain as I understood it. So I haven't taken the names for the purposes of my report from the ICMP list. I did take them from the ICRC -- sorry, from the ICRC list. I did take them from the ICMP and not ICRC. I didn't mix those two. It was not only the names which I used for my report were important on the ICMP list. There were site codes, case IDs, protocol IDs, these were all important information which I found out on these lists. None of these information, apart from missing person name and their date of birth, would appear on the ICRC list. If there were instances, for example, I needed to confirm something, where and when certain individual went missing, then I would consult the ICRC list. Because, simply, we did see yesterday that on the ICMP list for most of people the date of disappearance is 11th of July. But for the purposes of my report, let me emphasize again, the basic list which I used was the ICMP list. And there -- this is where I extracted the people, individuals, from, apart from those 35 which were identified before of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So let me be sure on my part. All that you did vis-a-vis the ICRC list was the process of checking whether the individuals identified by the ICMP were matching with the ICRC list. Am I correct in so understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That part was done by the demographic unit. I didn't -- I haven't been involved in this issue. And they will explain I think in detail what discrepancies they did find in relation to matching both lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I want to know which column in the ICMP list should be corrected to fit the elements of the ICRC list. Is it the place of disappearance - and we've seen that a large number disappeared in the woods - or is it the date? What must be amended in the ICMP list with the help of the ICRC list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify. These are two separate lists and they were created for two different purposes. And, you know, I don't want to go into the methodology how they were created, not even why, for example, the ICMP decided to put the date of disappearance as 11 of July rather than the exact date. So that's up to the institution who made up the list. So I don't think anything should be changed in relation that I can use in my report. Because what was important to compile my report were the entries which I explained in detail yesterday, and those entries would not appear on the ICRC list. So you cannot say particularly, yes, this should be amended or this should not be amended. Because for the purposes of my report, I don't need anything to be amended in these lists. For the -- for some other purposes of the accuracy in relation, for example, to the date of disappearance or place of disappearance, that's different issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So from which list should we take the date of disappearance and the place of disappearance to be associated with the DNA profiles with identifications?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would definitely consult the ICRC list in regards to this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But ICMP made its own list much later with much more information than the ICRC had.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's also my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Is this the only arbitrariness that you observe in the ICMP material?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say this is the most obvious one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These two columns, the date of death -- or rather, the date of disappearance and the place of disappearance?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are -- date and the place of disappearance are the most obvious, although I did spot some discrepancies also with the site name column, where, for example, site name would not be -- the name of the site would be different than the case ID would show us. And also many discrepancies within the site co-ordinate column, so where exactly certain grave was exhumed. So there were discrepancies in this data as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure I'm following the conversation. What did you mean by "obvious"? Mr. Karadzic referred to the date of disappearance and place of disappearance. Was the ICMP ever tasked with such -- finding such places and such date? And what did you mean by "obvious"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, they were never tasked to find exactly when and where exactly certain individuals went missing. What they were doing were they were trying to establish if they went missing after the fall of Srebrenica, if they're related to this event. What I meant by "obvious" is you can see clearly that from my experience before reviewing the ICRC list where you can see you have different date of disappearance for individuals and also place of disappearance, it was a little bit odd to me to find in the ICMP list that the date of disappearance is for every single person 11th of July and for -- as place of disappearance would be forest or Potocari I think, those two sites would be listed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you also take into account the third list, the certificates of death issued by Bosnian authorities which mostly indicate where the people disappeared? That's a third document.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say I did review some of those documents as well, I did see them, but they were analysed in detail by demographic unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So these demographic elements from your report and your testimony should not be taken for granted; we should wait for certification?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true because I know that they verified this data, demographic unit verified this data. And I relied my report also upon their conclusions, that numbers there are reliable. Individuals listed there who are identified are the ones who went missing after the fall of Srebrenica and that's why I consider this reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, what worries me is that there may be arbitrariness on your part as well because you move rather freely from document to document and then you choose like from a menu, we'll take this from this document because it suits the case of the Prosecution and from the other document we'll pick something else. Do you stand behind everything you've said and written?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why can't you answer these questions then? Why are you directing me to your demographers? What if they don't testify at all?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I answered that my report is based on the ICMP data, on the list compiled by the ICMP. This data were verified by demographic unit and that's why I rely -- relied on this data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Let me clarify that. Previously you said I rely -- referring to the demographic report in response to the question of Mr. Karadzic, you said: "I relied my report also upon their conclusions ..." Does it mean that you relied on ICMP report that has been verified by the demographic experts? Or did you rely on demographic experts' conclusion directly? If you could be more specific.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. What I meant was that I was -- I relied my report on the verifications made by demographic unit in relation to this report to the ICMP list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you be more specific as to the meaning of the verification made by demographics.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I have done -- what they have done, they compared to the -- the two lists, and they found - if I'm not mistaken - that most of the individuals which are on the ICMP list were included on the -- were also part of the ICMP [sic] list. And in addition, there were some additional names which didn't appear on the ICRC list. Through their further examination, I think they verified those additional individuals also as being part of the individuals who went missing after the fall of Srebrenica. So -- and that's what I was having in mind when saying "verification." So -- and this is explained in detail in their reports. So I would need to consult these reports for more -- for additional details, but it was long time ago when I checked this, their conclusions in their reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you did not do further than what demographic experts did in relation to ICMP list. Is there anything further that you did yourself than the demographic experts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put simply, then, you relied on the ICMP list, and the ICMP list can be verified when demographics come to testify. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I'm saying, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, I think we need to just make maybe one clarification before the transcript goes off. Page 8, line 3, the witness said on 2 "that most of the individuals which are," line 3, "on the ICMP list were included were also part of the ICMP list." I wonder if the individual meant originally, "were on the ICRC list were included on the ICMP list." I wonder if that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you follow, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. It should be ICRC list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So most of the individuals which are on the ICRC list were included or were also part of ICMP list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's true, but I have to come back to this. So you found a possibility for two columns in the ICMP papers to be questioned in comparison with the ICRC lists; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they show different data.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the ICMP list was updated compared to the ICRC. It's fresher, newer, later than the ICRC list.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ICMP list is more recent, of course, but if I'm not mistaken the ICRC list is also updated very often. So they are updating ICRC list as well. If they find discrepancies or they find individuals who were reported as went missing after the fall of Srebrenica - and that was not the case - these individuals are then taken off this list. So also the ICRC list is a live document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which version of the ICRC list did you use for comparison and decided that it was more accurate than the ICMP list from year 1995 or some other list?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it should be later than 1995. And it was, again, not me who compared this list. It was demographic unit who compared them, but I can be now specific as to which list was the one when I consulted them last.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that it never happened in any case that people were found. Do you know that people even came from Novi Sad, their names are on lists and on monuments, whereas they had been living in Serbia all the time, got married and led normal lives. Are you aware of such cases? People even came back from Germany, but let's just take Novi Sad which is much closer.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of this particular case. I do know that people were taken off the lists, but we can discuss individual cases if you wish so and we can take a look what the problem was, but about the Novi Sad case, I'm not particularly aware of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me now, how did the ICRC get its information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, I have to admit that I haven't analysed that area in detail. I do know that the information are coming from the relatives at the time when they reported their family members missing after the fall of Srebrenica, but in detail I haven't examined this list in respect to how they reported them missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, was there anything else you could have done other than rely on the verification of the demographic unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I did several other things, Your Honour. Not for all the cases, but there were sometimes discrepancies in the ICMP data which I could establish reviewing the site codes or case IDs. And in such cases where there was something -- according to my opinion something must be wrong, I checked, for example, this individual in other -- in our database or I would run search and try to find more information. And doing that, I think that I excluded, let's say, up to ten individuals from the ICMP list because they were not related to Srebrenica event. I found that they were -- that they died before in some other events, in 1992 and 1993, for example; and I excluded them. I haven't included them into my report. So I did try to verify this data also myself. Of course, it is too many individuals that you would be doing more every single one, but if there is a discrepancy which is obvious, or in my opinion was obvious, then I did run search and try to establish what the problem was. So I was trying to verify it myself as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency, for that clarification. It is useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, did you inform the ICMP about your objections in relation to these two columns?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to date and place of disappearance, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that too and also whether they lost their lives earlier on. I mean generally speaking, did you collate your findings to those of the ICMP and did you find any aberrations, if you will?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I informed the ICMP about my findings, and nowadays you will see these people are not included into their list anymore. They would be found in a separate column which says "not related to Srebrenica" or "excluded." But I'm not sure was this conclusion made by themself or because they were informed from our side that there is discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. So you think that the Red Cross found these names by interviewing relatives; right? What about the ICMP, how did they get their information about the names, places of disappearance, and dates of disappearance?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is the same. They do interview or they're trying more to locate the relatives of these individuals because they're trying to get as many blood samples from the relatives as possible in order to conclude or to identify particular individual. And doing that, of course, they have to approach relatives to create a database. So I think their approach is much more similar, but again in detail I don't know this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could a distant relative also report disappearance to the Red Cross or some official?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assume so, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, as for the ICMP a distant relative could not provide blood samples or information and an official couldn't do it either. It would have to be a person who was close to the missing person; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For sure not official unless he was a relative. It should be a close relative of course. So how close, it's again about the genetics and I would not go into that area because I'm not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Couldn't information -- shouldn't information provided by a close relative be trusted more than the Red Cross list that can be compiled from various sources, including distant ones?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depends. You have to go on a case-to-case basis and to see details as to who reported, when reported, how reported -- how close this individual was to that person who reported it missing and, you know, it all depends. You know, you have to go on a case-to-case basis. Because not always -- even if -- if it is a relative, for example, he wouldn't be able to report the place or date of disappearance because we have many cases when people were in a group walking through the woods together and they witnessed, you know, that certain individual went missing or was killed. So this is the more reliable source. For example, friend of that individual is more reliable source as to the place and date of disappearance than the relative who was not, for example, with this person at the time. So it all depends what you want to establish. So you can't say black or white this is more reliable than the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, since they were created before the ICMP list, were ICRC lists accessible to the ICMP and why did the ICMP not use them? Why did they try to get information of their own?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the ICMP -- if -- sorry, if the ICRC list was available to the ICMP. I don't know about that and how -- if it was available, they used that list. So that one, I don't know. But if they collected - I mean the ICMP - the information by themselves for verification purposes, I mean our OTP verification purposes, those two lists are better then because they are unrelated to each other. And if they match -- they both match, so then you have more reliable information about certain individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I have to intervene. I'm of the impression that we are wasting time in a sense. Mr. Janc, I'm asking you again whether ICMP was tasked to find out where the missing persons disappeared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. That was obviously not their task. Their task is to identify individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Karadzic, you didn't put these questions when Mr. Parson was here. So come to more relevant -- critical issues as to which Mr. Janc testified in his examination-in-chief. I should have said "Mr. Parsons" instead of "Parson."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the greatest respect, sir, Mr. Parsons did not question these two columns in his findings, but Mr. Janc did and the OTP did. It's as if they had a menu and they choose some columns from the ICMP and the two that they don't like they take from the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Had Mr. Parsons challenged that, I would have asked him.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. Mr. Parsons testified in regarding all the ICMP database. If Mr. Karadzic had chosen to question him about these particular two columns, he could have done so. We did not pick and choose which information should come through each witness in some method to bypass a cross-examination. If he wanted to talk about this information with the person who is best-placed to talk about it, he should have done so with Mr. Parsons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's come to more core issues, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that names are very important, or rather, of crucial importance for determining what the fate of a particular person was? For example, it is easy to establish a DNA profile if you have material, but do you have to link that up with the name of that particular person? That is to say, do you have to identify that person with the assistance of relatives or some yard-stick that is used?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that there are 260 profiles that haven't been identified yet. What does that mean, that they have not been identified yet? They have not been linked up to relatives; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. We don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, nevertheless you include them in the list of missing persons after Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because all of them, all of those 260, are found in mass graves, where we have identifications of only individuals who went missing after the fall of Srebrenica. It's logical inference then that all the others would be also related to that event. I'm quite confident to say, yes, they're related to the same event.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And after the fall of Srebrenica, all of those persons who were found in mass graves went missing; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, you yourself found about ten of those who were found in mass graves and who had lost their lives in 1992 and 1993. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those I found on the list, on the ICMP list, were not individuals buried or found in graves or in mass graves, let's put it this way. They were -- because the ICMP list is not only mass graves. I presented there also individuals which are found on the surface, for example, or in small graves. And those ten, let's put it this way, I found them being either on the surface or there was only one small grave, which I excluded as being Srebrenica related, but there were individual cases in these places. I haven't found a single one, a single person so far, in mass grave as being related to any other event than Srebrenica. The exception is Bljeceva 1 grave. There we have a slight problem because we know it's a mixed grave, and for that particular grave-site you will see that I have not included any unique DNA profile because for obvious reason. I cannot say is it 1992 or 1995 related exhuming site. Unless the only exception was to that grave if there was connection of this unique profile found in Bljeceva 1 to another grave-site, for example, Bljeceva 2 or Glogova, then it was again obvious to me that that individual came from Glogova site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since, Mr. Janc, you refer to this, let me come back to that issue. Shall we upload page 30 of Exhibit P4772, that's a public version of Mr. Janc's report which refers to Bljeceva grave. You said that's the only grave where the bodies not related to Srebrenica event were also buried or mixed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said this grave also contained the remains of bodies unconnected with the fall of Srebrenica. So what I wanted to be sure with you is that those numbers were not included in so-called unique profiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Were they identified at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. We have the names of 47, and those 47 are related to Srebrenica event and we have their names. The others --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, the other -- on -- those bodies unconnected with the fall of Srebrenica. Were they identified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They are identified, I think most of them, and the majority of the individuals within this grave are unrelated to Srebrenica. I think it's around -- at least when I last checked it, it was 90 individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How were they identified? Were they also included in ICRC list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they are not on the ICRC Srebrenica-related list. They would appear on other ICRC list, general list of all the people missing in war of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And they were not included into the ICMP list, Srebrenica-related list either. So we needed to check with the ICMP separately: Please give us the names of the individuals found in this grave unrelated to Srebrenica, and they provided us these 90 names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we get these names related to Bljeceva 1 and are not linked to Srebrenica 1995? Can we carry out our own investigation?
I'm sure those names will be, if not yet already, disclosed to you. But I cannot help you because I don't have access to this data anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure if Ms. West could help us in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we're -- we are talking about the names, this other 90-plus names, it is un -- number one, it's unclear to me at this point whether these would be disclosed to the Defence because these are not related to our case. And number two, even if we had these in our possession, we would certainly have to consult with ICMP as to their disclosure. So at this point, that is all I can say about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll leave it at that, but I would expect you to do your best to disclose that material, if you haven't, to the Defence. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So then we have to understand it this way, that in Bljeceva 1 there are bodies from different periods of time pertaining to different events; right?
Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your view, that the only grave in which there are bodies from different periods of time?
Yes, for these mass graves, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When completing your work, did you also rely on witness statements and other accessible material?
Yes, I did review many of such statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you notice that Mr. Erdemovic confirmed that at the time of these events he was informed by a guard at the farm that burials had taken place there earlier on as well, in the same place where they buried the victims of the 16th of July, 1995?
I don't have this particular statement of him in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For the participants, the transcript reference is 25387 and 388 from the testimony of Mr. Erdemovic in this case. During the interview you said that you had amended a list on the basis of information provided by a young girl who informed you that four victims were buried in Cerska. Do you remember that, the Cerska grave?
There were two young kids, not young girls. I do remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did they say?

Basically they were captured during this search of terrain around 16th of July, 1995, in the area of Pobudje along with other prisoners. They were transported back to Bratunac, and during their interviews they listed several people which were captured and taken prisoner along with them. Checking their names on the ICMP list, I found out that they ended up in Cerska grave. So they were taken from Bratunac to Cerska and executed. Those two young boys, they survived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Four men were taken to Cerska, killed, and buried not before the 16th of July; right?

You know, when I came across this information, I checked what kind of evidence we have on Cerska in relation to the exact date of execution. I found out that most probably it did not happen, that incident did not happen on 13th of July, but sometimes later, I would say around 17th of July. There were not only four individuals which were named by these boys which are found in Cerska grave. I found several other statements because I had been investigating this part a little bit more in detail, several other statements talking about other individuals who are found in Cerska grave, and from their statement I can conclude that they were also captured later than 13th of July, with this same incident, this same sweep operation. They were taken to Cerska and executed. I think I found about ten individuals from those different statements which are found in Cerska grave. Apart from that, I went further and I checked the exhumation records and what was found during the exhumation process. Because there might be some information which will point us at a date or something else. Yes, what I found, indeed, I checked the dates on the watches which were found inside the grave. And many of them would reflect or would stop around 18, 17, 18, 19 of whatever day, but I assume it's July. So that was additional fact which would point at my conclusion that these people were executed later than 13th of July. These are the main things, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Mr. Janc, this is the first time that the Defence is hearing this, that the 13th is being brought into question, although our position is that this had not happened on the 13th. I believe that this is the first time that the Trial Chamber is hearing this, that this had not happened on the 13th. And now I'm going to put my own case to you. Cerska and many other graves had multiple burials, and some of these burials are the result of sanitisation of the terrain; that is to say, no one can claim that all of these persons had been executed. Rather, in different ways and at different points in time they ended up in the very same grave. What do you say to that?
I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this kind of possibility exist? Can it be ruled out?

It's not black and white, again, and let me start with Kravica execution or actually Glogova primary grave. So inside this grave there are not only victims from Kravica execution. We know that other people were -- other bodies, actually, were brought into this grave, specifically one found in and around Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac, the ones from Konjevic Polje, a few of them, and mainly the ones picked up along the road, Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road. So those who were found lying -- being dead next to the road. And yes, we have such examples in that grave. Still, majority of them is related to Kravica execution. We have statements and we have people who testified here I think in this trial, saying that nobody dare to went into the woods to pick up these individuals who were killed there. So this is one exception. For the northern graves, let's put it this way, Branjevo, Orahovac, Petkovci, Kozluk execution points and primary graves, we don't have any evidence that people other than those executed are in those graves. Sanitation process did not really happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to that, but when you say "executions," those who were gathered by the road, were they also executed, shot, or were they killed in some other way? Has this been confirmed?

Of course it's difficult to confirm for every single individual who was killed, how he was killed, especially after long time. And we know that in the area where we have the vast majority of surface remains left on the ground, there were -- these people died of different causes. I don't dispute that there was some combat casualties, some people we know committed suicides because they didn't see any other way out, they were walking over minefields and some of them died because of this cause, and we also know that some of them were executed. So we have different causes of death in that area, but most of them - if not everybody - were just left behind, they were never picked up from the area. We know how many of them were so far identified, and we have evidence only those along the road, the main road, were collected and buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The ones who were killed in Kravica after the incident and after the chaos, or rather, the ones who died there, do you also consider these people to have been executed, been shot?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure it is for the witness to testify to that. It's also -- may be speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But the witness has analysed all the documents and he is well aware of the fact that there was an incident there, but no kind of execution had been prepared or planned. And what I'm interested in is whether he noticed that there was an incident that occurred in a chaotic situation, and this is significantly different from a planned and organised execution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you said that no one dared go into the forest and to take sanitation and hygiene measures. What were the reasons for which they didn't dare go there?

That was a statement of the individual who was involved in this process, in burial process, that they didn't dare to go there. What we know from documents, that there was a sweep operation in that area going on after 13th of July, and many of them -- of the people were executed during this operation. Not in combat, they were executed. And I'm particularly referring to this 17 -- let's say -- let's put it 17 July or 16 July 1995 incident around Burnice area with this same young kid being captured. When they surrendered the house or the building where they were hiding, you know, they killed, executed, many people there, the VRS forces and especially I think the police forces were engaged in that area, in sweeping that terrain. And this is coming out of the witness statement. So a lot is going on in that area at that time, but mostly it's related to search of the terrain. It's not done for sanitation purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you say that one person said that they didn't dare go into the forest. This had to do with taking sanitation and hygiene measures. Was that person from the military or from the civilian protection force?
He's from the civilian protection force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 65 ter 3966 in the e-court system. And I believe that there should be a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the order from Colonel Acamovic. We can see his signature or, rather, his name at the bottom. It's dated the 20th of July and it says -- it says on the basis of the demonstrated need and with the aim of locating and collecting human bodies and animal carcasses in the zone of responsibility of the units and burying them, internment, cremation, and of removing them, particularly in the areas of Srebrenica and Zepa and also Kamenica and Snagovo, everything which could be dangerous or harmful to the health of humans or animals preventing the contamination of water, food, soil, and air, and thereby guarding against contagious diseases of humans and animals. And then it says I hereby orders -- it issues an order according to which hygiene and sanitation measures should be taken. Do you think this was not done? Do you think this order wasn't carried out? Do you have any information that indicates that someone refused to abide by this order, or rather, to carry it out?

No, I have no such information, but when I was referring that no sanitation was done in area, I was referring to the all -- apparently all the mass graves were already closed. We know that from aerial images. And especially because I think this one is -- I didn't catch the area which is this referring to. But anyway, that would be my answer, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the area, the area of responsibility of certain brigades. Do you know which brigades were deployed in the area of the events in question from the 12th and 13th and onwards. Was the Bratunac Brigade there, the Zvornik Brigade, the Milici Brigade, the 1st Bircani Brigade, do we agree on this? The Milici and Bircani Brigade didn't suffer a significant attack, but the Zvornik and Bratunac Brigade did; isn't that correct? And you can see Snagovo, you know where Snagovo is. You also know where Kamenica is; isn't that correct? Right up to Zvornik, the entire area.
Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May I be heard on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I object to the admission of this document. This witness first of all said he has no such information. He went on to talk about testimony he had given earlier. This last piece of information as to the whereabouts of these particular brigades, that is just general information that this witness knows from his investigations. It has nothing to do with the substance of this document. I don't think this witness has confirmed any of its content and has made no positive comments about it. It doesn't fall within the Rules and I don't think it should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But it's relevant to the part of evidence he gave referring to his knowledge that there was no sanitisation in the area, and you don't have any doubt as to the content -- authenticity of this document, Ms. West?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: As to your second question, no, I don't. It's relevant that -- he's saying I think the opposite of this document. He's not making any positive comment about this document. He's not affirming its content. So -- and furthermore, he's an investigator. If this were a witness, a percipient witness from the time, I think that the Defence could come much closer, but this isn't a document for this investigator to get in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and I think maybe Mr. Tieger could even help me with this, but I think it's been our practice that when a document that's authenticity is not questioned directly contradicts the testimony of a witness, even though the witness doesn't confirm its contents, it's been admissible.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry to interrupt. I'll withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2216, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you the following. Do you agree that the source to determine the time and place of death of people found in the mass graves should be the ICMP, the International Red Cross, the list of the killed soldiers of the ABiH, and Court decisions certifying death, those were the four sources. Did you compare those four sources, did you analyse them?

I think I testified what was basis for my report in detail, and that it came across the list of killed soldiers and court decisions as well. And also they were examined by demographic unit as well. I'm aware of such documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at 1D4 -- 5487 in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, I'll show you part of our analysis from our investigation and also a result of the comparisons of certain texts, just part of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it please be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at it. These are examples found by various Defence teams. They compared these examples. In the first part of the list, you have the OTP list, the second part is the Army of BiH list, and the third part is the ICMP list. So have a look at the name. Avdo Ademovic, father's name Taib, born the 20th of September, 1968. Date of death, according to Brunborg, 12th of July, 1995. In the case of the ABiH, the date of death is the 1st of August, 1993. I have the ID protocol, 1192, and it's the Cancari mass grave. Then we have Dzemail Ahmetovic, number 2, father's name Dervis, born in 1977, date of death, according to the Prosecution, is the 13th of July. According to the ABiH, it's the 10th of January, 1994. The grave is Liplje, ID protocol 11826/08? The third in the list - I won't read out all the names - according to the Prosecution died on the 14th of July. According to the ABiH on the 18th of August, 1994. Protocol ID is 11635/8. Kamenica mass grave. And then number 4 you can see for yourself the date of death, 18th of August, 1994, and you can see the protocol ID, that column has been filled in. Number 5, 10th of January, 1994, is the time of death and it's in Ravnice and Hodzici. These are all mass graves.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here the first 2, 4, 6 names we can have a look at. I won't read all the names. Everyone can see the names from Alic and onwards. Time of death according to the Prosecution the 5th of June or August 1995. According to the ABiH, the 10th of January, 1994. And then we have another Alic, also the 10th of January, 1994. You have the protocol number and there's Hodzici Put grave number 5. And then we have Cancari and Zeleni Jadar and Zeleni Jadar again and Liplje, then Glogova. And in April 1993, the 17th of April, 1993, there's Bektic. And then we have a little lower down -- have a look at Bektic, who was found on the Hodzici Snagovo 3 road. He died on the 12th of December, 1992. And then see Cerska 68/02 is the protocol number. All these people --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at the next page in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- all these people were found in mass graves and none of them was connected to Srebrenica 1995, let alone to the executions. Please, have a look at all of them, 1992, 1992, then we have 1994, then we have 1993, 1992, 1994, 1994, 1994, 1992, 1994, and then we have Cancari, Ravnice, Kravica, Cancari, Cancari, Liplje, and so on. I won't read out all the names. So we can see that they are in Liplje, Cancari, Hodzici, Cancari 2, Cancari 3, Kamenica, Cancari 10, Glogova 2, Zeleni Jadar 5, Liplje 2, Bljeceva 2, Liplje 2, Liplje 4, Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the list. It's all in 1994, sometimes in 1992, then sometimes 1993. Omerovic is in 1993. I won't read the name, 1993 found in Hodzici road 5. So, Mr. Janc --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page so that everyone can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- the Defence claim is as follows. In that area people killed for three and a half years, 44 months, in fact. Those who died in enemy territory were buried in mass graves and that concerned the Serbs and the Muslims. In 1993 the Serbs discovered about 50 of their mass graves, where the Muslims had buried Serbs, and there were five to fifty corpses there. There were between -- there were 1.260 Serbian victims up until April 1993. On the other hand, up until that point in time, Muslims were also dying and almost exclusively on Serbian territory, and they were buried on Serbian territory up until July 1995. And in July 1995 there were a lot of people who were killed and they were buried in mass graves. If you haven't found individual graves of the thousands who were killed in the combat, then they were buried in mass graves. So how can we identify or associate mass graves with these executions by shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page, please. That's the last one in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can just interject here. If Mr. Karadzic can help us in regard to the source of this Army of BiH list. He said it was put together by Defence teams, but if we could have the source of the list, maybe an ERN, and when it was put together, it will be more helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have several lists from the ABiH. After the break, we will tender the list that contains the names, these names, and the dates. The ABiH made a list of the men that it lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then let's proceed. Are you able to answer the question, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me see. It was long. Let me comment on this list first, especially ABiH list. I know that this was examined by demographic unit again. If I'm not mistaken, this list was compiled in 2004 sometimes by the ABiH, so which is long time after the incident, after the Srebrenica event. And I think the credibility of this list was questioned, especially as to the methodology, how it was compiled. And with such lists, it's always important for what purposes it is compiled. And I think it was concluded -- no, it would be speculation, but I know that they didn't find that list reliable, I mean demographic unit, in relation to ABiH list for some purposes. So that's why I still consider all those people found in these graves as being victims of Srebrenica killings, Srebrenica event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In your knowledge, for what purpose were the ABiH documents filed -- compiled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have exact knowledge for what purpose. We have to take a look into that. But I know that it's sometimes important for relatives as to when certain person died, to get certain benefits from the government. So -- and this might be compiled for that purposes. So I don't claim that. It's just my opinion, what I think was the case in this list, but we would need to take a look into this issue further. And these individuals found in these mass graves, I would say, you know, it would actually contradict their list because I didn't go through all of them or -- to check the autopsy reports and photographs and everything how those people and where they were found, for example. Analysis can be done, I'm sure, to see exactly how those people and where they were found within graves. And if they are mixed with the portion of people which came from the secondary grave, it would be unlikely that one body would somehow squeeze into the huge pile of graves, which we know were exhumed from the primary site. So analysis can be done on every single case to see how they were found and where. If they're from some other incidents, one would expect these people being in this grave in some separate location because they were brought from somewhere else, for example, and would be put on the top or on the bottom or would be in one pile, but not within the grave scattered. Yeah. This would more show, making this analysis, that this list is not reliable because it shows quite opposite. People are found in the grave where we have Srebrenica victims. In the shape they are found we will be able to conclude, yes, they might have been killed with the same incident, with the same execution. So this way would be very easy to exclude them as being any other than Srebrenica victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, do you believe that the ABiH made a list of the losses it sustained on a daily basis?
No, I'm not aware of that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did your demographic unit come to the conclusion that the ABiH lists were not reliable, or did they conclude that they were not suitable for the Prosecution thesis?

Not really -- and I'm not sure now if these names are coming -- dates exactly -- especially are coming from one list or from several ABiH lists. I know that there were several attempts by the OTP to get those lists from ABiH army and those sources. So I'm not sure if this is one or two or even more sources combined together. But they did make these inquiries with them, also looking into the methodology and what was the basis and everything. But I cannot comment on their conclusions, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution be of assistance, given the ERN number that clearly shows that the Prosecution included this document in the EDS?
As I can see ERN on top of it, so it should be a Prosecution document, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes and -- but to enhance the probative value of this document, probably the Defence needs to tender the ABiH list themselves later on. Yes, this will be given number, and next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2217, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we need to put it under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. West, I don't think so, but if you could give some guidance.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We are looking up this ERN right now. Maybe after the break I can provide some more information as to whether it should be under seal or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, if it should be under seal -- I think -- my information was that this document was broadcast, and if so we need to redact it now. The feed --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- the video part.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, for sure I can -- I mean, I see that there are protocol IDs on it related to names, so I think there's going to be some issue here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. President. Unless this has been admitted publicly in another case which we don't really know right now, I think it's probably better to put it under seal pending the disposition of our motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's put it provisionally under seal and we'll come back to that in a more comprehensive way together with other documents and redact the video part where this document was broadcast. Yes, we'll take a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00. Just one matter. To be sure, Mr. Tieger, we are not hearing KDZ320 this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Dr. Karadzic has asked if the Chamber would consider allowing him to have this entire session to complete his cross-examination of this witness, and in support of that we'd like to point out that although he was led viva voce, the introduction of his reports into evidence creates more material than what was covered in the direct examination. And he will make every effort to keep his examination focused and also keep within the time-frames for the next two witnesses so that we can complete all of the witnesses this week, but he would like to have that additional time with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, that should be fair enough as long as he remains on relevant issues that should be dealt with this witness properly. Yes, I see the nodding of my colleagues. Please proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, when in your view did the first executions take place? When was the first execution after the fall of Srebrenica?
It's difficult to be precise, but let me focus on the first, biggest execution which took place. It was, in my opinion, definitely Kravica execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was towards the evening on the 13th of July; right?
Yeah, it would start around 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you say it began, isn't it true it also ended quickly, just after 5.00? It was described as an incident and general chaos. Did you accept that description of the event as it occurred after the rifle was grabbed and the Serbian policeman was killed?
Yes, evidence show that it started with that incident. For how long it lasted later on, it's not really known, but it went for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your corrigendum you confirmed that some of the people found in the mass grave that contained also the people killed at Kravica should not have been linked with this execution site; correct?
Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you said that most of the remainder of the 1200 people, most of the 1200 people described as victims from Kravica should be associated with the warehouse at Kravica. How many people were captured at Kravica and how many were killed in that incident?

It's difficult to give you a precise number, but as I concluded in my report vast majority would be still related to Kravica incident, those found in Glogova primary and related secondary graves. When I was trying to put up the figure how many others than Kravica related would be in Glogova grave, I was counting those picked up along the road around Bratunac school, Konjevic Polje, I came up to figure around 80 people. On top of it, there is 100 people, around 100 people, also killed at Bratunac stadium. We don't have clear evidence where those were buried. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm concerned about the way in which this line of questioning proceeds. I wonder whether this witness is a proper witness to deal with these matters. That may open the Prosecution to explore with the investigators as to the matters that was dealt with in the indictment, which we prohibited. Do you have any observation, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I agree with you that it's a slippery slope for us; on the other hand, the identity of the bodies that were found in the mass graves and where they were killed is something pretty directly relevant to this witness's testimony. So perhaps Dr. Karadzic can focus his questions more narrowly on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robinson. Please advise Mr. Karadzic to that effect. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll say very briefly, Mr. Janc. On the photographs on the footage and according to the information we received, we see that at Sandici and along the road there were from several dozen to 200, 250 prisoners. But according to our information at Kravica there were only 150. So this figure was multiplied practically by 10. I'm just asking: You did not verify these figures, you just accepted them from previous documents; right ?

No. What we can see actually on the video is not everything what happened in the area unfortunately because it's just a certain part of the day what is there. So we don't have any evidence as to what happened during the entire incident -- actually video evidence. And from other evidence we know that many or people were brought into the Kravica warehouse. We have survivors from this site saying how many people were brought there in different instances into this warehouse and then executed. And we know from the video that the one who surrendered, for example, we identified these people. That not all of them who surrendered at that time were killed at Kravica. Some of them are found in northern execution sites, Pilica, Orahovac, so they were transported somewhere else. So I would not even conclude that those we can see on video, on Petrovic video being at Sandici, that they were all killed at Kravica. Because it's clearly we have evidence that some of them ended up somewhere else. We know that buses came, also buses, and some of them were transported somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be more inclined to rely on the aerial photograph of the people that can be seen there at the time around 2.00 or 3.00 between Konjevic Polje and Kravica, including Sandici? Would you rely on that and the information as to the number of these prisoners?

Definitely aerial image would be one source of those -- of information. The problem with aerial image is it's always -- they are not focused enough for us to be able to count how many individuals is there. It's just an estimate and it might be fairly wrong estimate. So you can't really estimate from those pictures how many people is gathered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Concerning what you said, that the first executions on a larger scale took place on the 13th of July, I would like to show you a telegram from General Tolimir -- I think this is P4762. Can you recall that telegram where General Tolimir notifies on the 13th of July that there is enough place for 800 prisoners at Sjemece near the farms?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not P4769? 65 ter 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly. Maybe I misnoted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you recall that?
Yes, I do recall that document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know in the area of which brigades did most deaths of Serbian and Muslim soldiers occur?
No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the Bratunac and Zvornik Brigades were the most exposed to attacks, they had the most contact with the column?
If you are now referring to time after the fall of Srebrenica, then my answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call P3975, map number 5, page 14. Thank you. Could we zoom in. If I may ask the usher to help Mr. Janc mark the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark Pobudje, Buljim, and that whole area where you established that there were the most surface remains unburied. Could you put a circle around the area of Buljim and Pobudje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you not zoom in a bit further? Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe if you can zoom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One step further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, one step, it would be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can do once again, once more, and then just -- I think that can be done -- that will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The column started from Susnjari and Jaglici. Could you now put a circle around what is called Pobudje. There's Buljim and Pobudje.
Yes. Let me mark it as P.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your knowledge, how long did the column spend in that area? When did it leave?

The bulk of the column, I think a few days. But there were certain individuals that remained in this area for quite a long time up until 17th, 18th, or 20th of July. So not everybody were passing through at the same time so they split it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that this -- that the bulk of the column left this area maybe even on the first day and moved further on, outside the area of Pobudje?
I think they spent, the most of them, at least one night in this area but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see any report from the intelligence service of the BH army of the 17th of July, saying that on the 16th of July 10.000 fighting men from the 28th Division arrived to the free territory, so they successfully passed through and reached free territory. Did you see that report?
Yes, I do remember that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If that is the bulk of the column which should have passed through on the 16th, there were between 13th and 15th, 15.000 in all and 10.000 managed to arrive at the free territory, can we consider that between the 12th and the 16th the bulk of the column were between this circle you marked and Nezuk, the separation line?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, what is the meaning of these green lines that run straight in certain sections and sometimes meander along the river? Are these areas of responsibility of two brigades, the Bratunac Brigade to the south and the Zvornik Brigade to the north?

It's a little bit difficult for me to comment on this because I am not originator of this map. But those green lines would correspond, to my knowledge, as to where the boundaries of those two brigades were, yes. If they're exact, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now please put the date and your initials on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, I did some quick calculations in connection with the schedule. I simply wanted to note - and the Court may already be aware of this - that if everything proceeded perfectly as scheduled without any re-direct or without any administrative matters, we would still conclude at the end of the week with only 15 minutes to spare. That's cutting it pretty close it seems to me. So at a minimum, maybe the Court wants to consider more, I think we have to conclude this witness with his -- with any re-direct examination by the end of this session, and the Court may want to consider whether it's willing to cut it that close in light of its previous concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Having heard Mr. Tieger's submission, please try to conclude your cross-examination as early as possible, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing missing is how much time is necessary for re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it you have re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I do and I think it will be five minutes, but at least five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Try your best, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will. Thank you. Could this map be admitted and then we need to turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2218, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please, of this same document, P3975.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You would like to see the next map, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It should have a separate 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I think we already admitted the next page too under the same P number, P4770, 65 ter 4799. 65 ter 4779, page 15 and 16. I thought it was in the same exhibit. P4770, admitted yesterday. I saw it with my own eyes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with this and you marked these surface remains; correct?
Yes, I'm aware of this map, but it was not me who put these dots on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that a representative of the civilian protection who said he did not dare go into the forests was in this area where we have the most surface remains?
Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Janc, in this area of Pobudje, which was the area of the Bratunac Brigade, the bulk of the column numbering 13- to 15.000 people stayed much less time than in the rest of this area until the separation line, and 500, maybe 600 surface remains remained unburied. In the rest of the territory in this sector were the greatest losses, both Serb and Muslim. Why didn't we find there more surface remains than in Pobudje? What happened to them?

Now what happened to them -- to who? To surface remains which we don't know if they were ever there. What we know from the exhumations is how many of them were found at which location, and the majority is in Pobudje area. Then we have a small cluster around Snagovo, and then we have around 60 of them found in Baljkovica area. So we know in Baljkovica there was a battle when they were trying -- the Muslim column was trying to break through. Corridor was later opened, and still we did find many of them just on the ground. The majority, of course, is in Pobudje area, and it's difficult to me to say where those are because I don't know if there were any at the time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's the problem, Mr. Janc. Most of the unburied remains were found in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade. However, most of the dead are in the area of the Zvornik Brigade. There's no denying that. That's where the fiercest fighting took place, went on for four days. Where are the casualties from the fighting in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade?

Definitely we have 60 of them there, on this map. They're marked and they're part of my report as being surface remains. Those were never buried. Then where are the others if they were, I don't know where they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know -- or rather, did you see this information, namely, that the Zvornik Brigade that was in shelters, in trenches, behind heavy weaponry, sustained losses between 40 and 50 in a single day? What is your assumption then? The Muslims who are out in the open and who were advancing, how many casualties had they sustained? What is the usual ratio, 1:7? 1:8? Isn't that right?
It's more for military expert than me, so I would not be able to answer this question because it would be a pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But can you tell us the following then -- actually, could you please take a pen and could you mark this, where the Bratunac Brigade was and the rest of the area up to Nezuk.
You would like me first to mark the area of Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do, yes, where Pobudje is -- or Pobudje itself, whatever you prefer.
I'd say this and mark it with P would be Pobudje area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that the rest of the area on the other side of the river, all the way up to Nezuk, is the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade? Could you please put a circle there, including the area between the Bratunac and Zvornik Brigades, including the surface remains.
Let me put Z next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Janc, isn't it obvious that many more surface remains were found at Pobudje where they spent a night and half a day rather than in the area of the Zvornik Brigade, where they spent four days in the fiercest fighting?

They also spent many more days - let me emphasize this first - I mean Pobudje area -- not the majority perhaps, but many people were still there up to 20th of July, so it's seven, eight days even. And yeah, we have less of them found on the surface in Bratunac area and Snagovo area than Pobudje area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were less found in the area of the Zvornik Brigade, as shown by this map?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that the secret service of the BH army reported that between 13- to 15.000 men from the column passed already on the 16th?
Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put the date there and your initials.
[Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, as Exhibit D2219.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D5493.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is my case, Mr. Janc, that there were more deaths in the area of the Zvornik Brigade and less surface remains. So that means that while the terrain was cleared up they were buried. Apart from these mass graves, were any other graves found in which those who got killed during those four days in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade had been buried?

Yes, indeed. There are several graves, but they're all small ones in this area and in Baljkovica area. You will find them in my report, and I would attribute those people to the incidents to this fight, whatever happened in this Baljkovica area. And I will just list the graves --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Can we please hear whether this can be broadcast? Actually, just in case, perhaps it shouldn't be broadcast. Do go on, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those graves are Brzlog [phoen] grave, where we have five individuals identified; and Motovska Kosa, four; and then Krizevici, nine. So these are three main ones. Then we have some individual graves as well, like Seher-Osmaci, from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find a grave with hundreds of casualties from this fighting?
Not yet, but many of them are still on the missing list. So maybe in the future there will be one of such grave discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And maybe they were buried in the existing graves during the clearing up of the terrain?

I would exclude that because evidence shows that they were opened and closed in very short period of time. I think the last one is closed in -- on 17th of July. In order to go around the terrain and collect all the bodies, it would take a lot of effort and -- to bring them back to the -- to those mass graves, it would take much more time than just one day to exhume -- to make the hole for or to prepare the grave for bodies and to put them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we have any aerial images taken during a single day or several days?

I would need to consult them exactly, but I know they have -- we had them from several days, different locations several days, or even for one location several days. But I'm not sure. I would need to go through them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If Colonel Acamovic on the 20th of July issued an order for burials as part of sanitisation, would they have been completed by the 27th of July?

No, an order itself, it doesn't mean that sanitisation happened. You know, I would rather, in this respect, see the reports about what's going on on terrain. Because order might be issued and changed later the day with another report.
